source.title: SAE-RNA: A Sparse Autoencoder Model for Interpreting RNA Language Model Representations

record.tranche_reason: The study reports sparse features in a new RNA language-model setting, but also explicitly limits claims that these features are stable or definitive biological units.
record.gate_note: The study trains SAEs on RiNALMo representations and reports feature-to-annotation alignments and layer-wise activation patterns, which bear on V4 and, for the reported stability limitation, V5. It does not test superposition geometry, capacity competition, or feature dimensionality. Feature counts shown only in Figure 2 are not extracted as findings because the text provides no corresponding values.
record.test_reason: The study applies SAEs to a new kind of model, the RNA language model RiNALMo. It reports that selected dictionary features align with sequence, structure and RNA-family annotations, which bears on V4 in a new setting. It is not T5: it gives no quantitative result that any version is wrong. Its stability remark rests on unreported preliminary experiments. Evidence is weak: features are hand-selected subsets, labelled with GPT-5 help, and compared against no baseline.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors frame SAE-RNA as exploratory. Selected features align with known sequence, structure and family annotations, and deeper layers are more type-selective. They do not claim definitive biological concepts, and they flag feature stability, length normalization, hyperparameter sensitivity and signal-versus-noise validation as unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains overcomplete sparse autoencoders on RiNALMo RNA-language-model embeddings and aligns their activations with biological annotations; it does not reproduce the original toy-network experiments or test their geometric claims.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that feature-level conclusions may depend on the sparsity penalty, activation threshold, top-k selection, aggregation method, and layer selection; they do not systematically vary these choices.
record.problems: The study uses 10k RNA sequences for SAE training and says scaling to millions could broaden coverage. It notes dependence on annotation quality and analysis choices, unresolved normalization for variable-length sequences, possible noise or thresholding artifacts in activation spikes, and insufficient feature stability and validation. Several conclusions are qualitative and based on selected features and heatmap visualizations.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 shows retained feature counts by layer, but the text does not state the values. No rows were otherwise left out.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweeps or geometry.
No neuron polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
No comparison of SAE features with raw neurons. No evidence that features are spread across neurons. No quantitative interpretability or coverage over the whole dictionary.
Completeness, stability across seeds or dictionary sizes, and canonicality are not measured. Only an unquantified remark on downstream stability is made.

missing.what: Retained feature counts per layer after the at-least-10-sequences filter; values appear only in the figure
SAE reconstruction loss per layer (layer 1 visibly higher) and effective sparsity (mean active features per token); monitored but not reported numerically

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. I changed the tranche from T5 to T3: the stability remark is unquantified, so it gives no V5 verdict. All feature rows are hand-selected 'subset' table entries with GPT-5-assisted labels. There is no control (random features, raw neurons, base-rate structure composition), so support for V4 is weak.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-over-capacity sweep, overlap or near-orthogonality measurement, or sparsity-dependent transition.
No test of neuron polysemanticity, feature competition for capacity, or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
Tests SAE-derived features in RiNALMo, an RNA language model, but not feature spreading across neurons or other LLMs.
Reports limitations concerning stability and biological interpretation, but does not systematically test feature completeness or canonicality.
No comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: RiNALMo
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE activation patterns across RiNALMo layers for RNA-type-selective channels.

conditions.value: 5 features per RNA type; normalized per feature and max-aggregated

rows.measure: Sparsity and RNA-type selectivity of activation patterns
rows.value: Layer 1 is described as having the lowest sparsity, with diffuse and widely shared activations.
rows.note: This is a relative qualitative comparison across layers, not a numerical sparsity measurement.
rows.check: Read only from normalized, max-aggregated top-k heatmaps. 'Sparsity' here is visual, not a reported metric. The pattern also depends on the aggregation choice.

rows.subject: RiNALMo
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE activation patterns across RiNALMo layers for RNA-type-selective channels.

conditions.value: 5 features per RNA type; normalized per feature and max-aggregated

rows.measure: Sparsity and RNA-type selectivity of activation patterns
rows.baseline: Layer 1 is described as the lowest-sparsity reference.
rows.value: Layer 18 and later are described as markedly sparser, with strong peaks on a small subset of channels per RNA type.
rows.note: The paper says the higher sparsity and selectivity remain elevated from layer 18 onward.
rows.check: Qualitative heatmap reading only. The authors note max aggregation makes late-layer selectivity visually salient.

rows.subject: RiNALMo
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE activation patterns across RiNALMo layers for RNA-type-selective channels.

conditions.value: 5 features per RNA type; normalized per feature and max-aggregated

rows.measure: Sparsity and RNA-type selectivity of activation patterns
rows.baseline: Layer 1 is described as the lowest-sparsity reference.
rows.value: Layer 33 is included in the reported later-layer pattern of markedly sparser, more type-selective activations.
rows.note: The paper reports mild fluctuations through layer 33, while describing the pattern as remaining elevated.
rows.check: Qualitative heatmap reading only. Mild fluctuations are noted.

rows.subject: RiNALMo
rows.operation_detail: Reported the authors' assessment of preliminary feature-activation stability and suitability for downstream interpretation.

conditions.value: Preliminary synthetic motif-perturbation and mutation-associated motif extensions

rows.measure: Stability and validation of SAE feature activations for reliable downstream conclusions
rows.value: The authors say the current feature activations were not sufficiently stable, normalized, or validated to support reliable downstream conclusions.
rows.note: The text does not provide a quantitative stability test or specify a stability metric.
rows.check: This is an author statement about unreported preliminary experiments, with no metric or values. It concerns using activations for downstream markers, not stability of SAE features across seeds or sizes. It cannot ground a verdict.

relationships.condition: Hand-selected layer-9 and layer-18 SAE features, and deeper-layer (L18–L33) activations, in RiNALMo
relationships.reason: Selected features show clear sequence runs with dominant structural contexts (R1-R4, R6-R14). Deeper-layer features are type-selective (R17-R18). No baseline was used and the features were cherry-picked subsets.
relationships.display_finding: Selected features showed clear sequence runs with dominant structural contexts, and deeper-layer features were type-selective. No baseline was used and the features were cherry-picked.

relationships.reason: Features 8004 and 10216 show no dominant structure (R5, R15). Layer 1 activations are diffuse and widely shared (R16).
relationships.display_finding: Features 8004 and 10216 showed no dominant structure, and layer 1 activations were diffuse and widely shared.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
